lessons: Open a long proof record with a short reading guide: the result, the mechanism in two or three sentences, what the record adds, who each part is for, and a table separating the required proof path from optional routes and evidence, each cell linked.
Begin every major section with one sentence saying where it is going before any definition or technical step.

At a statement-first formal entry point, give each central claim its configured target, its implementation, and whether the formal statement is the same as the claim, stronger, or weaker/partial, with how it differs; mark relations whose review is not current.

Every proof destination that another document links to should open with the statement it proves and its hypotheses, plus a one-line route back to the citing document; when a link must land mid-argument, put an arrival note at the anchor.
Keep run chronology, packet labels and receipt history in one evidence appendix; at each mathematical endpoint keep only the statement, premises, evidence category and a link.
Mark alternative proofs, refinements and literature forensics as optional where they occur, or move them to appendices with their anchors, so the required path reads continuously.
When a displayed equation-numbering convention mixes source and local labels, state the rule at the start and give a crosswalk rather than a blanket sentence.

Verify rendered navigation (PDF link annotations, destinations, file actions) on the actual output; anchor existence in the source does not prove a working link, and a correct anchor can sit behind a wrong label.
